article.title: Why a Stable Average Can Hide Customer Migration
article.why: Use transition analysis when stable aggregates hide movement between customer groups.

paragraphs.en:
A business dashboard can look reassuring when an average barely changes from one year to the next. Average annual spending may remain near 180,000 yen, or average purchase frequency may stay around 5.5 visits per month. It is tempting to conclude that customer behavior is stable. Yet the same average can be produced by very different customer movements.

Suppose half of a customer base increases spending while the other half decreases by a similar amount. The overall average may remain unchanged even though many customers have changed materially. For a membership program, this matters because customers moving upward may need a different strategy from customers drifting downward. An aggregate average cancels the two movements and hides both opportunities.

A useful solution is transition analysis. Assign customers to the same spending bands, deciles, or ranks in each period and build a transition matrix. Rows represent the previous period and columns the current period. The diagonal shows customers who stayed in the same group. Cells above or below it reveal upward and downward migration.

However, interpretation requires care. If ranks are recalculated independently each year, a customer can move in absolute spending without changing rank. For example, a customer may increase annual spending from 150,000 to 165,000 yen but remain in the same decile because the whole distribution moved upward. Conversely, someone can move to a better percentile even while spending less if other customers decline more. Therefore, analysts should compare both relative rank and absolute behavior.

Customer entry and exit create another complication. A matrix restricted to customers observed in both periods is excellent for studying same-customer movement, but it excludes new and lost customers. A complete report should therefore show the transition matrix for common customers and separate summaries for entrants and exits. This prevents retention changes from disappearing behind a clean-looking migration table.

The size of a movement also matters. Moving from one decile to the next may represent a tiny monetary change near a boundary or a large behavioral shift. Add absolute changes in spending and frequency, or calculate the distance to relevant rank thresholds. This helps distinguish boundary noise from meaningful migration.

For management, a concise statement might be: ‘Average annual spending was nearly flat, but only 42% of common customers stayed in the same spending band; 31% moved up and 27% moved down.’ That description reveals dynamics that the average cannot show.

Stable aggregates are not evidence of stable customers. Whenever the business cares about retention, rank-up, or deterioration, ask how individual customers moved beneath the summary statistic. The average describes the center of the population; a transition view describes the journey of its members.
paragraphs.zh:
商業 dashboard 中，如果平均值年度間幾乎不變，看起來往往令人安心。例如平均年度消費維持在18萬日圓附近，或平均購買頻率仍約每月5.5次，很容易因此認為顧客行為穩定。然而，相同平均值可能由完全不同的顧客移動所形成。

假設一半顧客增加消費，另一半以近似幅度減少，整體平均可能完全不變，但大量顧客其實發生了實質變化。對會員制度而言，往上移動與往下滑落的顧客需要不同策略；aggregate average 會把兩種變化互相抵消，也把兩邊的機會一起藏起來。

一個有用的方法是 transition analysis。用相同的 spending bands、deciles 或 ranks 對兩期顧客分類，建立 transition matrix。列代表前一期，欄代表本期；對角線表示留在同一群的人，對角線上下的格子則顯示 upward／downward migration。

但解讀要小心。如果每年都獨立重算 rank，顧客絕對消費改變也可能 rank 不變。例如年度消費從15萬增加到16.5萬，但整體 distribution 同時上移，所以仍在同一 decile。反過來，如果其他人跌得更多，某人即使消費下降，也可能 percentile 上升。因此應同時比較 relative rank 與 absolute behavior。

新客與流失客又增加一層複雜性。只限制兩期皆存在的 common customers 所做的 matrix，很適合研究 same-customer movement，但會排除 new 與 lost customers。完整報告應同時提供共通顧客 transition matrix，以及新進與退出顧客的獨立摘要，避免 retention 變化被漂亮的 migration table 掩蓋。

移動幅度也很重要。從一個 decile 到下一個，可能只是剛好跨過 boundary 的小金額變化，也可能是很大的行為改變。可以加入消費金額與頻率的 absolute change，或計算距離 rank threshold 的差額，以區分 boundary noise 與 meaningful migration。

向管理層報告時可以說：「平均年度消費幾乎持平，但共通顧客只有42%留在同一消費帶，31%上移、27%下移。」這比單一平均值更能呈現動態。

穩定的 aggregate 並不能證明顧客穩定。只要業務關心 retention、rank-up 或 deterioration，就應追問摘要數字底下每位顧客如何移動。平均值描述群體中心，而 transition view 描述成員的旅程。
paragraphs.ja:
business dashboardで平均値が前年差ほぼゼロだと安心してしまいがちです。年間平均利用額が18万円前後、平均購入頻度が月5.5回程度で変わらなければ、顧客行動は安定しているように見えます。しかし同じ平均値でも、その背後では全く異なる顧客移動が起きている可能性があります。

顧客の半分が利用額を増やし、残り半分が同程度減らせば、全体平均は変わりません。それでも多くの顧客には大きな変化があります。会員programでは上昇顧客と下降顧客で必要な施策が違うため、aggregate averageは両方向を相殺し、機会を隠してしまいます。

有効なのがtransition analysisです。各期間で同じspending band、decile、rankへ顧客を割り当てtransition matrixを作ります。行を前年、列を当年とすれば、対角線は同じgroupに残った顧客、上下のcellはupward／downward migrationを表します。

ただし解釈には注意が必要です。rankを毎年独立に再計算すると、絶対利用額が変わってもrankが同じ場合があります。15万円から16.5万円へ増えてもdistribution全体が上がれば同じdecileに残ります。逆に他顧客がもっと減れば、自分の利用額が減ってもpercentileが上がることがあります。そのためrelative rankとabsolute behaviorの両方を見るべきです。

新規・離脱も重要です。両期間に存在するcommon customerだけのmatrixはsame-customer movementを見るのに適していますが、新規と離脱を除外します。完全なreportでは共通顧客のtransition matrixに加え、entrantとexitを別に集計し、retention変化を隠さないようにします。

移動幅も確認します。decileを一つ跨いでもboundary付近の小さな金額差かもしれません。利用額・頻度のabsolute changeやrank thresholdまでの距離を加えれば、boundary noiseとmeaningful migrationを区別できます。

経営報告なら「年間平均利用額はほぼ横ばいですが、共通顧客で同一利用帯に残ったのは42％、31％が上昇、27％が下降しました」と説明できます。平均だけでは見えない動態です。

aggregateが安定していても顧客が安定しているとは限りません。retention、rank-up、deteriorationが重要なら、summary statisticの下で個々の顧客がどう移動したかを確認しましょう。平均はpopulationの中心を、transitionはその構成員の移動を示します。

business.term: The average is flat, but customer migration is substantial.
business.explanation: 平均持平但內部遷移很大時的實務表達。
